Definition: from G2288 to kill (literally or figuratively):--become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify.
BiblicalUsage: thanatóō stands behind the English phrase to put to death. In Matthew 10:21, the brother shall deliver up the brother to death. The word turns up 11 times, and each time it points to the same reality.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that putting sin to death is not God’s cruelty but His mercy, because what kills me must die in me. That is why thanatóō stays with me long after the verse is closed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
